question: Find the value of 69−⁴ ÷ 69¹⁰ × 69−¹⁷.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For operations on the same base, calculate the net exponent directly using BODMAS principles.

Net Exponent = (First Power) − (Divisor Power) + (Multiplier Power)

Net Exponent = −4 − 10 + (−17) = −31

**∴ The correct answer is 69−³¹.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

69−⁴ ÷ 69¹⁰ × 69−¹⁷

**Formula Used:**

am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ

am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

**Calculation:**

⇒ 69−⁴ ÷ 69¹⁰ × 69−¹⁷

⇒ (69−⁴ − ¹⁰) × 69−¹⁷

⇒ 69−¹⁴ × 69−¹⁷

⇒ 69−¹⁴ ⁺ ⁽−¹⁷⁾

⇒ 69−³¹

**∴ The correct answer is 69−³¹.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product and Quotient Rules of Exponents

When multiplying expressions with the same base, add their exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ. When dividing, subtract the exponent of the denominator from the numerator: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ.

Negative Exponent Rule

A negative exponent indicates the reciprocal of the base raised to the absolute value of the exponent: a−ⁿ = 1 ÷ aⁿ.

Zero Exponent Rule

Any non-zero base raised to the power of zero always equals one: a⁰ = 1.
